verses.zh: 他们来到海那边格拉森人的地方。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they came to the other side of the lake, to the region of the Gerasenes.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate a summary and transition in the narrative.

The region of the Gerasenes would be in Gentile territory on the (south)eastern side of the Sea of Galilee across from Galilee. Matthew 8:28 records this miracle as occurring “in the region of the Gadarenes.” “Irrespective of how one settles this issue, for the [second and] Third Evangelist the chief concern is that Jesus has crossed over into Gentile territory, ‘opposite Galilee’” (J. B. Green, Luke [NICNT], 337). The region of Gadara extended to the Sea of Galilee and included the town of Sennabris on the southern shore—the town that the herdsmen most likely entered after the drowning of the pigs.tc The textual tradition here is quite complicated. Most later mss (A C ƒ13 M syp,h) read “Gadarenes,” which is the better reading in Matt 8:28. Other mss (א2 L Δ Θ ƒ1 28 33 565 579 700 892 1241 1424 al sys bo) have “Gergesenes.” Others (א* B D latt sa) have “Gerasenes,” which is the reading followed in the translation here and in Luke 8:26. The difference between Matthew and Mark (which is parallel to Luke) may well have to do with uses of variant regional terms.

verses.zh: 耶稣一下船，就有一个被污鬼附着的人从坟茔里出来迎着他。
verses.en: Just as Jesus[NOTE:1] was getting out of the boat,[NOTE:2] a man with an unclean spirit[NOTE:3] came from the tombs and met him.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
See the note at Mark 1:19 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Unclean spirit refers to an evil spirit.

Grk “met him from the tombs a man with an unclean spirit.” When this is converted to normal English word order (“a man met him from the tombs with an unclean spirit”) it sounds as if “with an unclean spirit” modifies “the tombs.” Likewise, “a man with an unclean spirit from the tombs met him” implies that the unclean spirit came from the tombs, while the Greek text is clear that it is the man who had the unclean spirit who came from the tombs. To make this clear a second verb, “came,” is supplied in English: “came from the tombs and met him.”

verses.zh: 那人常住在坟茔里，没有人能捆住他，就是用铁链也不能；
verses.en: He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him anymore, not even with a chain.

verses.zh: 因为人屡次用脚镣和铁链捆锁他，铁链竟被他挣断了，脚镣也被他弄碎了；总没有人能制伏他。
verses.en: For his hands and feet had often been bound with chains and shackles,[NOTE:1] but[NOTE:2] he had torn the chains apart and broken the shackles in pieces. No one was strong enough to subdue him.
notes: Grk “he had often been bound with chains and shackles.” “Shackles” could also be translated “fetters”; they were chains for the feet.
Grk “and.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 他昼夜常在坟茔里和山中喊叫，又用石头砍自己。
verses.en: Each night and every day among the tombs and in the mountains, he would cry out and cut himself with stones.

verses.zh: 他远远地看见耶稣，就跑过去拜他，
verses.en: When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.

verses.zh: 大声呼叫说：「至高　神的儿子耶稣，我与你有甚么相干？我指着　神恳求你，不要叫我受苦！」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he cried out with a loud voice, “Leave me alone,[NOTE:2] Jesus, Son of the Most High God! I implore you by God[NOTE:3]—do not torment me!”
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

Grk “What to me and to you?” (an idiom). The phrase τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί (ti emoi kai soi) is Semitic in origin, though it made its way into colloquial Greek (BDAG 275 s.v. ἐγώ). The equivalent Hebrew expression in the OT had two basic meanings: (1) When one person was unjustly bothering another, the injured party could say “What to me and to you?” meaning, “What have I done to you that you should do this to me?” (Judg 11:12, 2 Chr 35:21, 1 Kgs 17:18). (2) When someone was asked to get involved in a matter he felt was no business of his own, he could say to the one asking him, “What to me and to you?” meaning, “That is your business, how am I involved?” (2 Kgs 3:13, Hos 14:8). These nuances were apparently expanded in Greek, but the basic notions of defensive hostility (option 1) and indifference or disengagement (option 2) are still present. BDAG suggests the following as glosses for this expression: What have I to do with you? What have we in common? Leave me alone! Never mind! Hostility between Jesus and the demons is certainly to be understood in this context, hence the translation: “Leave me alone….”

Though it seems unusual for a demon to invoke God’s name (“I implore you by God”) in his demands of Jesus, the parallel in Matt 8:29 suggests the reason: “Why have you come to torment us before the time?” There was an appointed time in which demons would face their judgment, and they seem to have viewed Jesus’ arrival on the scene as an illegitimate change in God’s plan regarding the time when their sentence would be executed.

verses.zh: 是因耶稣曾吩咐他说：「污鬼啊，从这人身上出来吧！」
verses.en: (For Jesus[NOTE:1] had said to him, “Come out of that man, you unclean spirit!”)[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
This is a parenthetical explanation by the author.

verses.zh: 耶稣问他说：「你名叫甚么？」回答说：「我名叫『群』，因为我们多的缘故」；
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] asked him, “What is your name?” And he said, “My name is Legion,[NOTE:2] for we are many.”
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The name Legion means “thousands,” a word taken from a Latin term for a large group of soldiers. The term not only suggests a multiple possession, but also adds a military feel to the account. This is a true battle.

verses.zh: 就再三地求耶稣，不要叫他们离开那地方。
verses.en: He begged Jesus[NOTE:1] repeatedly not to send them out of the region.
notes: Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 在那里山坡上，有一大群猪吃食；
verses.en: There on the hillside,[NOTE:1] a great herd of pigs was feeding.
notes: Grk “mountain,” but this might give the English reader the impression of a far higher summit.

verses.zh: 鬼就央求耶稣说：「求你打发我们往猪群里，附着猪去。」
verses.en: And the demonic spirits[NOTE:1] begged him, “Send us into the pigs. Let us enter them.”
notes: Grk “they”; the referent (the demonic spirits) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶稣准了他们，污鬼就出来，进入猪里去。于是那群猪闯下山崖，投在海里，淹死了。猪的数目约有二千。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] gave them permission.[NOTE:2] So[NOTE:3] the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs. Then the herd rushed down the steep slope into the lake, and about 2,000 were drowned in the lake.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Many have discussed why Jesus gave them permission, since the animals were destroyed. However, this is another example of a miracle that is a visual lesson. The demons are destructive: They were destroying the man. They destroyed the pigs. They destroy whatever they touch. The point was to take demonic influence seriously, as well as Jesus’ power over it as a picture of the larger battle for human souls. There would be no doubt how the man’s transformation had taken place.
Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate a conclusion and transition in the narrative.

verses.zh: 放猪的就逃跑了，去告诉城里和乡下的人。众人就来，要看是甚么事。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] the herdsmen ran off and spread the news in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate a transition to the response to the miraculous healing.

verses.zh: 他们来到耶稣那里，看见那被鬼附着的人，就是从前被群鬼所附的，坐着，穿上衣服，心里明白过来，他们就害怕。
verses.en: They came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting there, clothed, and in his right mind—the one who had the “Legion”—and they were afraid.

verses.zh: 看见这事的，便将鬼附之人所遇见的和那群猪的事都告诉了众人；
verses.en: Those who had seen what had happened to the demon-possessed man reported it, and they also told about the pigs.

verses.zh: 众人就央求耶稣离开他们的境界。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] they began to beg Jesus[NOTE:2] to leave their region.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶稣上船的时候，那从前被鬼附着的人恳求和耶稣同在。
verses.en: As he was getting into the boat the man who had been demon-possessed asked if he could go[NOTE:1] with him.
notes: Grk “be,” that is, “remain.” In this context that would involve accompanying Jesus as he went on his way.

verses.zh: 耶稣不许，却对他说：「你回家去，到你的亲属那里，将主为你所做的是何等大的事，是怎样怜悯你，都告诉他们。」
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] did not permit him to do so. Instead, he said to him, “Go to your home and to your people and tell them what the Lord has done for you,[NOTE:3] that he had mercy on you.”
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Jesus instructs the man to declare what the Lord has done for him, in contrast to the usual instructions (e.g., 1:44; 5:43) to remain silent. Here in Gentile territory Jesus allowed more open discussion of his ministry. D. L. Bock (Luke [BECNT], 1:781) suggests that with few Jewish religious representatives present, there would be less danger of misunderstanding Jesus’ ministry as political.

verses.zh: 那人就走了，在低加坡里传扬耶稣为他做了何等大的事，众人就都希奇。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis[NOTE:2] what Jesus had done for him,[NOTE:3] and all were amazed.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “So” to indicate the conclusion of the episode in the narrative.

The Decapolis refers to a group of towns (originally consisting of ten; the Greek name literally means “ten towns”) whose region (except for Scythopolis) lay on the east side of the Jordan River. Although frequently seen as a league of independent city states organized by the Roman general Pompey, contemporary sources do not support such a view. Rather their unity came from their Greek (Hellenistic) culture and religions, which set them apart from surrounding areas.
Note that the man could not separate what God had done from the one through whom God had done it (what Jesus had done for him). This man was called to witness to God’s goodness at home.

verses.zh: 耶稣坐船又渡到那边去，就有许多人到他那里聚集；他正在海边上。
verses.en: When Jesus had crossed again in a boat[NOTE:1] to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him, and he was by the sea.
notes: See the note at Mark 1:19 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

verses.zh: 有一个管会堂的人，名叫睚鲁，来见耶稣，就俯伏在他脚前，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] one of the synagogue leaders,[NOTE:2] named Jairus,[NOTE:3] came up, and when he saw Jesus,[NOTE:4] he fell at his feet.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

The synagogue was a place for Jewish prayer and worship, with recognized leadership. See also the note on synagogue in 1:21. tn That is, “an official in charge of the synagogue”; ἀρχισυνάγωγος (archisunagōgos) refers to the “president of a synagogue” (so BDAG 139 s.v. and L&N 53.93; cf. Luke 8:41).

Codex Bezae (D) and some Itala mss omit the words “named Jairus.” The evidence for the inclusion of the phrase is extremely strong, however. The witnesses in behalf of ὀνόματι ᾿Ιάϊρος (onomati Iairos) include P45 א A B C L M lat sy co. The best explanation is that the phrase was accidentally dropped during the transmission of one strand of the Western text.
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 再三地求他，说：「我的小女儿快要死了，求你去按手在她身上，使她痊愈，得以活了。」
verses.en: He asked him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Come and lay your hands on her so that she may be healed and live.”

verses.zh: 耶稣就和他同去。有许多人跟随拥挤他。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around him.
notes: Grk “He”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 有一个女人，患了十二年的血漏，
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] a woman was there who had been suffering from a hemorrhage[NOTE:2] for 12 years.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

This probably refers to a chronic vaginal or uterine hemorrhage which rendered the woman ritually unclean, thus limiting her social contacts and religious participation (see further J. Marcus, Mark 1–8 [AYB], 357).tn Grk “a flow of blood.”

This story of the woman who had been suffering from hemorrhages for 12 years is recounted in the middle of the story about Jairus’ daughter. Mark’s account (as is often the case) is longer and more detailed than the parallel accounts in Matt 9:18-26 and Luke 8:40-56. Mark’s fuller account may be intended to show that the healing of the woman was an anticipation of the healing of the little girl.

verses.zh: 在好些医生手里受了许多的苦，又花尽了她所有的，一点也不见好，病势反倒更重了。
verses.en: She had endured a great deal under the care of many doctors and had spent all that she had. Yet instead of getting better, she grew worse.

verses.zh: 她听见耶稣的事，就从后头来，杂在众人中间，摸耶稣的衣裳，
verses.en: When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “garment,” but here ἱμάτιον (himation) denotes the outer garment in particular.

verses.zh: 意思说：「我只摸他的衣裳，就必痊愈。」
verses.en: for she kept saying,[NOTE:1] “If only I touch his clothes, I will be healed.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfect verb is here taken iteratively, for the context suggests that the woman was trying to muster up the courage to touch Jesus’ cloak.

In this pericope the author uses a term for being healed (Grk “saved”) that would have spiritual significance to his readers. It may be a double entendre (cf. parallel in Matt 9:21 which uses the same term), since elsewhere he uses verbs that simply mean “heal”: If only the reader would “touch” Jesus, he too would be “saved.”tn Grk “saved.”

verses.zh: 于是她血漏的源头立刻干了；她便觉得身上的灾病好了。
verses.en: At once the bleeding stopped,[NOTE:1] and she felt in her body that she was healed of her disease.
notes: The woman was most likely suffering from a vaginal or uterine hemorrhage, in which case her bleeding would make her ritually unclean.tn Grk “the flow of her blood dried up.”

verses.zh: 耶稣顿时心里觉得有能力从自己身上出去，就在众人中间转过来，说：「谁摸我的衣裳？」
verses.en: Jesus knew at once that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”

verses.zh: 门徒对他说：「你看众人拥挤你，还说『谁摸我』吗？」
verses.en: His disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing against you and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

verses.zh: 耶稣周围观看，要见做这事的女人。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] he looked around to see who had done it.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 那女人知道在自己身上所成的事，就恐惧战兢，来俯伏在耶稣跟前，将实情全告诉他。
verses.en: Then the woman, with fear and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.

verses.zh: 耶稣对她说：「女儿，你的信救了你，平平安安地回去吧！你的灾病痊愈了。」
verses.en: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well.[NOTE:1] Go in peace, and be healed of your disease.”
notes: Or “has delivered you”; Grk “has saved you.” This should not be understood as an expression for full salvation in the immediate context; it refers only to the woman’s healing.

verses.zh: 还说话的时候，有人从管会堂的家里来，说：「你的女儿死了，何必还劳动先生呢？」
verses.en: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader’s[NOTE:1] house saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any longer?”
notes: See the note on synagogue leaders in 5:22.

verses.zh: 耶稣听见所说的话，就对管会堂的说：「不要怕，只要信！」
verses.en: But Jesus, paying no attention to what was said, told the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”

verses.zh: 于是带着彼得、雅各、和雅各的兄弟约翰同去，不许别人跟随他。
verses.en: He did not let anyone follow him except Peter, James,[NOTE:1] and John, the brother of James.
notes: Grk “and James,” but καί (kai) has not been translated since English normally uses a coordinating conjunction only between the last two elements in a series of three or more.

verses.zh: 他们来到管会堂的家里；耶稣看见那里乱嚷，并有人大大地哭泣哀号，
verses.en: They came to the house of the synagogue leader where[NOTE:1] he saw noisy confusion and people weeping and wailing loudly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “and,” though such paratactic structure is rather awkward in English.
This group probably includes outside or even professional mourners, not just family, because a large group seems to be present.

verses.zh: 进到里面，就对他们说：「为甚么乱嚷哭泣呢？孩子不是死了，是睡着了。」
verses.en: When he entered he said to them, “Why are you distressed and weeping? The child is not dead but asleep!”

verses.zh: 他们就嗤笑耶稣。耶稣把他们都撵出去，就带着孩子的父母和跟随的人进了孩子所在的地方，
verses.en: And they began making fun of him.[NOTE:1] But he forced them all outside,[NOTE:2] and he took the child’s father and mother and his own companions[NOTE:3] and went into the room where the child was.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “They were laughing at him.” The imperfect verb has been taken ingressively.

Or “threw them all outside.” The verb used, ἐκβάλλω (ekballō), almost always has the connotation of force in Mark. The typical “put them all outside” is somewhat understated in the context; given the raucous nature of the crowd in v. 38, forceful activity was probably required in order to evict them.
Grk “those with him.”
Grk “into where the child was.”

verses.zh: 就拉着孩子的手，对她说：「大利大，古米！」（翻出来就是说：「闺女，我吩咐你起来！」）
verses.en: Then, gently taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha koum,” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up.”

verses.zh: 那闺女立时起来走。他们就大大地惊奇；闺女已经十二岁了。
verses.en: The girl got up at once and began to walk around (she was twelve years old). They were completely astonished at this.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek word εὐθύς (euthus, often translated “immediately” or “right away”) has not been translated here. It sometimes occurs with a weakened, inferential use (BDAG 406 s.v. 2), not contributing significantly to the flow of the narrative. For further discussion, see R. J. Decker, Temporal Deixis of the Greek Verb in the Gospel of Mark with Reference to Verbal Aspect (SBG 10), 73-77.

verses.zh: 耶稣切切地嘱咐他们，不要叫人知道这事，又吩咐给她东西吃。
verses.en: He strictly ordered that no one should know about this,[NOTE:1] and told them to give her something to eat.
notes: That no one should know about this. See the note on the phrase who he was in 3:12.
